info.name: Student Information Management API
info.description:
REST API collection for the Student Information Management API (Laravel 12 + Sanctum).

Base URL is `/api/v1`. Authentication uses a Sanctum bearer token.

How to use:
1. Select the `Student API (local)` environment.
2. Run the `Authentication` folder first (top to bottom). `Login (admin)` saves `{{token}}`, and the other logins save `{{student_token}}`, `{{instructor_token}}`, and `{{instructor2_token}}`.
3. Run the remaining folders in order. Every create request saves the new id into an environment variable (for example `{{student_id}}`) so later requests chain automatically.
4. Folders include both successful and deliberately failing requests (401, 403, 404, 409, 422).

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Login, current user, and logout. Also demonstrates 401 responses and token revocation.

request.description: Authenticates as the seeded Administrator and saves the token to {{token}}.
Authenticates as the seeded Student and saves the token to {{student_token}}.
Authenticates as Instructor One (the owner of the offering created later) and saves {{instructor_token}}.
Authenticates as Instructor Two (not the owner of the created offering). Used to demonstrate 403.
Wrong password must return 422 and never reveal whether the email exists.
Returns the authenticated user using the collection's bearer token ({{token}}).
Protected endpoint must reject an unauthenticated request with 401.
Issues a throwaway token so the logout test does not revoke the main {{token}}.
Revokes the temporary token.
After logout, the revoked token must no longer work (401).

item.name: 2. Students
item.description: CRUD, search, filter, sort, pagination, validation, and object-level authorization for students.

request.description: Partial-match search across name fields, student number, and email.
Exact-match filters plus an allow-listed sort field and direction.
Pagination metadata: current_page, per_page, total, last_page, from, to.
Creates a student. {{program_id}} defaults to a seeded program id (1). Saves {{student_id}} and {{student_number}}.
Retrieves the student created above.
Partial update; only supplied fields change.
Reuses the student number just created; the unique rule must reject it.
Invalid email must fail validation and must not be saved.
A non-existent id returns 404, not an HTML error page.
Object-level authorization: changing the URL id must not expose another student's record.
Creates a disposable student so the delete example does not remove the chained {{student_id}}.
Deletes the disposable student.

item.name: 3. Programs
item.description: CRUD, lifecycle, and dependency protection for programs.

request.description: Lists programs.
Creates a program. The code uses {{$timestamp}} so re-runs stay unique. Saves {{program_id}} and {{program_code}}.
Retrieves the program created above.
Updates the program.
Reuses the code just created to prove the unique rule works.
Program 1 is seeded with students, so deletion is refused with 409 instead of orphaning rows.
Creates a disposable program with no students.
Deletes the disposable program.

item.name: 4. Courses
item.description: CRUD and validation for the course catalog.

request.description: Lists courses.

body.raw:
{
  "course_code": "TC{{$timestamp}}",

request.description: Creates a course and saves {{course_id}} and {{course_code}}.
Retrieves the course.
Updates the course.
Reuses the course code just created.
Creates a disposable course with no offerings.
Deletes the disposable course.

item.name: 5. Academic Terms
item.description: CRUD and the unique (academic_year, semester) rule.

request.description: Lists academic terms.
Creates a term and saves {{academic_term_id}}, {{academic_year}}, {{semester}}.
Retrieves the term.
Updates the term.
The (academic_year, semester) pair was just created, so the unique rule rejects it.
Creates a disposable term with no offerings.
Deletes the disposable term.

item.name: 6. Course Offerings
item.description: Sections of a course in a term, taught by an instructor. Includes instructor scoping.

request.description: Lists offerings (admin sees all).
An instructor only ever sees their own offerings — the server adds the filter, the client cannot opt out.
Creates an offering taught by {{instructor_id}} (default 3 = instructor@example.com). Saves {{course_offering_id}}.
Retrieves the offering with its course, term, instructor, and enrollment count.
Nested route listing the offering's enrolled students.
Updates the offering.
The instructor must be an existing user whose role is instructor — a plain user id or missing id is rejected.
Creates a disposable offering with no enrollments.
Deletes the disposable offering.

item.name: 7. Enrollments
item.description: Enrolling students into offerings, including duplicate protection.

request.description: Lists enrollments (admin sees all).
Enrolls {{student_id}} into {{course_offering_id}}. Saves {{enrollment_id}}.
Retrieves the enrollment with its student, offering, and grade.
Updates the enrollment status.
The same student in the same offering is prevented (unique constraint + service check).
A student_id that does not exist must fail validation.
A student may not list the whole enrollment table.
Enrolls a different seeded student (id 2) into the same offering, so it can be deleted.
Drops the extra enrollment, leaving the main one for the Grades folder.

item.name: 8. Grades
item.description: Grade entry and instructor-level authorization. Grades are updated, never deleted.

request.description: Lists grades (admin sees all).
Creates a grade for {{enrollment_id}}. `remarks` is derived by the model (90 => PASSED).
Retrieves the grade.
Administrator can update any grade.
Instructor One teaches the offering, so the grade is theirs to edit.
Instructor Two does not own this offering, so the grade is off-limits.
A grade must reference an existing enrollment.
One grade per enrollment: a second grade for the same enrollment is refused.

item.name: 9. Academic Records
item.description: A student's academic record grouped by academic term, with object-level authorization.

request.description: Administrator reads student 1's record, grouped by academic term.
The demo student account is linked to student 1, so it can read its own record.
Changing the id to another student must return 403 — object-level authorization.
